hyps.why: When the learning rate is tiny, the network is under-trained after 243 epochs, so a larger step helps a lot.
Learning rates near 1 make Adam diverge or stall, so going higher hurts more than at moderate rates.
Reducing an excessive learning rate restores stable training.
With a low learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and even more under-training.
Smaller batches give more update steps, which helps when the learning rate is too small to converge.
Small batches add gradient noise, which combined with a high learning rate destabilizes training.
A very strong L2 penalty near 1 over-regularizes and underfits.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening already wide ones.
Deeper ReLU nets are more fragile at high learning rates and are more likely to diverge or die.
Wider layers amplify the effective update size, so high learning rates become more unstable.
